failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed-recipe supervisor never moves the setpoints (0 m travel in the bad runs), so it cannot use the free split degree of freedom. A feed draw-off from tank1 (or a pump1-gain / split shift) forces the off-diagonal h1 PI loop to saturate pump2 (v2 -> 12 V), which drives h3 above the 0.75 m limit for hundreds of seconds (853 s in feed_step, 588 s in combined_step). No adaptation to pump-gain loss or split shift, so saturations and upper-level violations persist.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the model-based split but make the split law explicitly track the estimated disturbance and pump gains across calls and add gentle production reduction only when the h3 cap and h2 band conflict.

self_check: The supervisor reconstructs the unmeasured feed draw-off (d1,d2) and each pump's effective gain from the clean upper-tank mass balances in the window, then uses the linear steady-state relation between the lower-tank outflows and the pump voltages to predict v1 and v2 for any candidate h1/h2 split. It searches the feasible split interval that keeps predicted v2 below the value giving h3 = 0.95*limit (and v1 below the h4/saturation cap) and h2 inside its band, and returns the pair closest to the current setpoints so it does not move more than needed. When h3 is pushed toward its limit the split is shifted toward tank2 (lower h1, higher h2), which lowers v2; when a pump saturates the predicted-voltage cap forces the split toward the healthy pump. Only if no split satisfies both the h3 cap and the h2 band does it reduce production slightly, since lost production (1/L) is cheaper than upper-limit violations (2/s).
proposed_change: Replace the fixed-recipe scaling with a model-based split supervisor that estimates pump gains and feed draw-off online and picks the h1/h2 pair meeting production while keeping predicted pump voltages, hence h3/h4, inside limits.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The fixed-recipe supervisor ignores disturbances, so when feed draw-off or combined pump/split shifts push one lower tank to demand more flow, the paired pump saturates and the corresponding upper tank (h3 or h4) exceeds the 0.75 m limit for hundreds of seconds, causing large constraint penalties.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use the steady-state mass balances to estimate effective upper-tank flow gains and unmeasured lower-tank disturbances from telemetry, then choose the production split that keeps predicted h3, h4 and pump voltages inside safe margins while meeting the production target with minimal setpoint travel.

self_check: My supervisor estimates effective upper-tank flow gains and unmeasured lower-tank disturbances from the latest sample. It scans the one degree of freedom (production split) to predict required pump voltages and upper levels, and selects the split that keeps production on target while maintaining h3, h4 and pump voltages below safe margins with minimum setpoint travel. If a pump saturates or an upper level approaches its limit, the cost function shifts production toward the other tank until the constraint margin is restored.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed recipe with a model-based supervisor that infers disturbances from telemetry and scans the production split to satisfy Q and constraints. The scan penalizes predicted upper-level and pump-saturation violations and setpoint travel, returning the nearest safe split.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor is a fixed recipe that never uses its free degree of freedom, so it cannot react when a disturbance forces a lower-tank PI loop to push its pump. In dev_feed_step_0 an extra draw-off from tank1 (d1=-1.16 L/s) makes the h1 loop (driving pump 2) run v2 up to its 12 V ceiling; because 80% of that flow goes to tank3, h3 climbs past the 0.75 m limit (853 s of violation). The same mechanism appears in the combined pump-loss/split-shift scenarios (588-398 s), and pump saturation plus upper-tank level rise also degrades dev_pump_sine and the ramp cases.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the disturbance-residual estimator and constrained (h1,h2) optimiser; if scores still show transient upper-level overshoot, increase the h3/h4 soft-margin threshold or shorten the residual window for faster reaction, without adding a stored state.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the active feed disturbances (and any pump-gain/split change) from the exact mass-balance residuals of the telemetry window, then solves the steady-state pump equations for every candidate production split between the two lower tanks. It keeps Q on target by construction (h2 is derived from the target once h1 is chosen) and shifts production from tank1 to tank2 whenever the predicted h3 would approach its limit, and from tank2 to tank1 whenever h4 or v1 would. When a pump must saturate, it picks the split that keeps the predicted upper levels just under the limit and the pumps below their voltage ceiling, trading a little production only when no feasible split exists.
proposed_change: Add model-based disturbance estimation (feed flows plus effective pump/split gains from the tank balances) and a one-dimensional constrained search over the production split h1/h2 that minimises setpoint travel subject to upper-level, pump-voltage, band and safety limits.

failure_analysis.what_failed: A fixed open-loop recipe never moves the setpoints, so when a feed draw-off pulls tank1 down, the h1 PI loop drives pump2 (which feeds tank3 through the off-diagonal 0.8 split) to saturation, pushing h3 far above its 0.75 m limit for hundreds of seconds. The production curve alone cannot avoid this; the free split degree of freedom is never used.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Compute the current inflow into each upper tank from level plus slope, predict its steady level, and continuously re-split production along the constant-Q curve so the binding upper level is pulled back while respecting the h2 band and the pump voltage limits.

self_check: The returned setpoints always lie on the Q = Q(h1)+Q(h2) = target curve, so once the low-level loops settle the reported production is on target by construction. For each upper tank I estimate the current inflow as a*c*sqrt(h) + dh/dt, whose square gives the steady level if the pump voltage is held; if that prediction approaches the 0.75 m limit I shift production toward the other lower tank along the curve. The shift is bounded so h2 stays in its band and v1, v2 stay off saturation, and it is applied with a damped gain so transient inflation of the inflow estimate cannot cause over-travel.
proposed_change: Predict each upper-tank steady level from the measured level and its slope, then shift production between tank1 and tank2 along the constant-production curve in the direction that relieves the binding upper-tank constraint, clamped by the h2 band, safety limits and pump-voltage margins, applied with a damping factor.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor forecast the steady upper levels from the upper tank's pump-side inflow (a*c*sqrt(h)+dh/dt) instead of its outflow, so during loop transients it mis-predicted where h3/h4 settle: it under-reacted when a feed draw-off raised h3 (113 s above 0.75 m in dev_feed_step_0) and it moved the split for spurious reasons in the oscillating scenarios. The extra dref term biased the split toward tank2 whenever total production was low, the 0.8 damping weakened the constraint response, and the level/pump limits were blended rather than solved, producing large production off-target integrals (332-396 L) in the sine scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the model-based split search but estimate the lower-tank net inflow (a*c*sqrt(h)+dh/dt minus the upper-tank outflow) to observe the disturbance and direct pump flow online; solve the coupled steady-state balances for h3/h4 and pump voltages for every candidate split and pick the split with least setpoint travel that satisfies the upper-level, band, pump and safety limits, with no extra heuristic bias.

self_check: For every candidate split the code solves the two coupled lower-tank steady-state balances using the disturbance estimated from the measured levels and slopes, giving predicted h3, h4, v1 and v2; it then picks the split that keeps these inside [1.3, 11.6] V and below the upper-level target while moving the setpoints as little as possible. Because shifting production to tank2 always lowers v2/h3 and raises v1/h4, the scan automatically trades upper-level headroom against the h2 band and pump saturation, so a saturating pump or a rising upper level forces exactly enough shift. Production stays on target because every candidate satisfies Q1+Q2=Q_target by construction; when both upper limits cannot be held, the weighted cost selects the least-violating split and a deadband suppresses needless moves.
proposed_change: Replace the inflow-based upper-level forecast and dref heuristic with a disturbance estimate taken from the lower-tank balances and a one-dimensional scan over the production split that minimises setpoint travel subject to predicted h3/h4, h2-band, pump-voltage and safety limits.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor predicts the effect of a production shift with fixed nominal cross-coupling coefficients and never anchors its prediction on the measured pump voltages, so it reacts late: h3 runs above 0.75 m for 113 s in dev_feed_step_0 and pump1 saturates for 92 s in dev_split_step_0. Its own constraint correction is then damped by a 0.8 factor, the free split is re-planned from scratch every call (churn on the pump sine: 0.39 m), and the target step is handled by a fixed recipe that over-moves the setpoints (0.63 m) and leaves 140-400 L of production error.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the measurement-anchored, ratcheting split (move only when a predicted constraint binds, then hold) and verify on held-out timing that the h3 cap margin and the pump-voltage cap do not trade too much production error for too little setpoint travel.

self_check: The split delta is only allowed to move when a predicted constraint binds, so an upper level nearing its cap (h3 or h4 predicted above 0.71 m) or a pump voltage nearing 11.7 V pushes delta in the relieving direction and it is then held, which stops the supervisor from chasing oscillations. Predicted steady states are anchored on the measured v1, v2 and on the measured upper-tank inflows a*c*sqrt(h)+dh/dt, so the coefficients that shift with a pump-gain or split disturbance are re-identified every call and the correction aims at the true steady state rather than at the nominal one. The production constraint Q1+Q2 = target is enforced exactly by construction, so moving the split never moves production off target, and the h2 band, safety limits and setpoint limits are enforced as hard penalties inside the same one-dimensional search.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed-coefficient recipe with a one-dimensional constrained search over the production split whose steady-state prediction is anchored on the measured pump voltages, holding the current split unless a predicted upper-level, band, safety or pump-voltage violation forces a move. Cap h3/h4 predictions at a margin below the limit and cap the pump voltages below saturation so the correction is applied in full rather than damped.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor holds setpoints too long and derives its one-dimensional delta shift from a fixed split ratio and a damped inflow estimate, so on step disturbances it ignores the real feed draw-off, lets h3 run over 0.75 m, and on sine disturbances it chases the oscillation with setpoint travel without reducing the production error.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the scalar delta recipe with a steady-state model-based split search that uses exact mass-balance estimates of the feed flows and effective pump gains, and pick the min-travel split that keeps predicted h3, h4, h2 and pump voltages feasible.

self_check: Each call reconstructs the unmeasured feed flows and the effective pump gains from the 50 s window via exact tank mass balances, then predicts the steady h3, h4 and pump voltages for every candidate (h1,h2) split. The cost heavily penalises h3/h4 above the limit, h2 outside its band, pump saturation and production error while charging 100 per metre of travel, so the supervisor only moves setpoints when the physics demands it. If a binding constraint forces a conflict it lets production deviate slightly (cheaper per second than a constraint violation) and keeps the split as close to the current setpoints as possible.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed-recipe delta shift with a steady-state optimal split search that estimates feed flows and effective pump gains from mass balances and minimises constraint violations plus production error plus setpoint travel.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor's admissible-interval bounds are driven by the instantaneous level slope, so brief h3/h4 transients chatter the split setpoints (travel and extra production transients, e.g. dev_pump_sine_0, dev_feed_sine_0, dev_combined_sine_0), while genuinely persistent violations (dev_feed_step_0, h3>0.75 for 113 s) get only a small, slow 0.075 m correction. Pump limits are enforced only at 11.7 V, too late to stop the level sag and production loss when a pump gain drops.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the projection-based split logic but re-tune the rate limit, voltage cap and level margins on held-out scenarios, and check the split-disturbance case where the feed estimate is biased by the assumed gamma.

self_check: The supervisor moves the split only when a steady-state projection says an upper tank or a pump will hit its margin: it estimates the feed draw-off from the tank-1/tank-2 mass balances and the effective pump gains from each upper tank's measured inflow, then solves analytically for the split that keeps predicted infl3/infl4, h3/h4 and v1/v2 inside their limits. When nothing projects to a limit it holds the target-derived setpoints, so production stays on target and no travel is spent on transients. A level guard using the measured inflow catches an actual h3/h4 excursion, and moves are rate-limited so the loops can follow smoothly. Conflicts (e.g. h2 band vs h3 limit) are resolved by taking the midpoint inside the safety interval.
proposed_change: Replace the slope-driven soft bounds with a steady-state projection built from the estimated feed disturbances and effective pump gains, add a v1/v2 margin cap, rate-limit the split and drop the baseline anchor when a limit binds. Enforce the h2 band and safety limits as hard bounds and keep a gradient guard from the measured upper-tank inflow.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Heuristic delta shift chatters setpoints and fails to keep production on target under oscillatory disturbances; upper limit violated on feed step.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use window-averaged effective gains and disturbances to predict steady-state upper levels and pump voltages, then scan the production split to minimize travel subject to constraints, holding setpoints when feasible.

self_check: The supervisor estimates effective pump gains and feed disturbances from the telemetry window, then scans the one-dimensional split between tank1 and tank2 along the production-target curve. For each candidate it predicts steady-state upper levels and pump voltages; if predicted peaks exceed limits or pumps saturate, it shifts production to the other tank while keeping total Q on target. If the current setpoints are feasible, it holds them to avoid transients.
proposed_change: Replace the heuristic delta shift with a steady-state constrained scan over the production split, using effective gains and disturbances estimated from the window.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor used an incorrect coupling factor (0.8/0.6 instead of 0.25) and a fixed pump-voltage gain, so it mispredicted how setpoint shifts affect upper levels and pump saturation. It moved setpoints during sine disturbances even when no constraint was threatened, injecting tracking transients that caused large production errors; conversely, it under-shifted during pump-gain loss, allowing pump saturation and h3 limit violations.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the fixed-recipe delta with a scan over the production split that estimates lower-tank disturbances and effective pump gains from window mass balances, then chooses the split minimising setpoint travel subject to predicted h3/h4, h2-band, and pump-voltage limits.

self_check: The supervisor estimates current effective pump gains and lower-tank disturbances from the mass balances using level slopes. For each candidate setpoint pair it solves the steady-state upper-tank balances to predict required h3, h4 and pump voltages, then selects the pair closest to the active setpoints that keeps h3/h4 below the limit and both pumps away from saturation. If a disturbance pushes an upper level toward its limit, the scan shifts production toward the other tank just enough to bring the predicted level back under the limit; if a pump approaches saturation, the scan shifts production away from that pump until the predicted voltage falls below the safe cap. Unnecessary moves are avoided because the active setpoints are kept unless a predicted constraint violation forces a change.
proposed_change: Use a steady-state projection based on estimated disturbances and effective pump gains, and scan the one-dimensional production split for the minimal-travel setpoint pair that satisfies all predicted constraints.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor chased production transients with setpoint moves and used a fixed nominal-scaled anchor, causing large setpoint travel and long recovery on pump and feed sine disturbances, and allowed h3 to exceed its limit during a feed step because the upper-level soft bound left too little margin.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Anchor the split on a minimal-travel point of the production contour and only shift when a projected steady-state constraint (upper level, h2 band, pump cap) binds.

self_check: The setpoints returned always lie on the steady-state production contour Q1(h1)+Q2(h2)=Q_target, so the base PI loops hold production on target regardless of feed, pump-gain or split disturbances until a pump saturates. When a projected upper level approaches its limit, the code shifts the split along the contour toward the other pump, which lowers the offending upper-tank inflow; when a pump voltage nears its cap, the same shift relieves that pump. If the h2 band would be violated, the shift is clipped to the band edge, and only the truly infeasible cases leave residual production error.
proposed_change: Replace the nominal-scaled setpoint anchor with a scan along the Q=target contour that minimises L1 setpoint travel from the current pair, and tighten the projected upper-level target to 88% of the limit so the split shift acts earlier.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor reacted to every disturbance with a fixed recipe that shifts the production split using an approximate upper-tank inflow forecast. On feed draw-off steps this under-corrected and let h3 sit above 0.75 m for 113 s (226 points), and on sine disturbances it kept nudging the setpoints, so the level loops chased a moving target and the production integral grew (up to 400 L) while the split no longer reflected the projected limits.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Estimate the delivered pump flows and the lower-tank disturbances from the mass balances (including dh/dt), then hold the active setpoints unless a projected steady-state h3/h4, h2-band or pump-voltage limit is breached; search the constant-production curve only when a breach is projected.

self_check: Each call I recover the actual pump2/pump1 delivered flows from the h3 and h4 mass balances (a*c*sqrt(h)+dh/dt divided by 1-gamma), which gives the effective pump gains and the lower-tank disturbances with no steady-state assumption. Using those, I solve the two steady mass balances for any candidate (h1,h2) and predict the resulting h3, h4, v1 and v2. If the active setpoint pair already keeps the predicted upper levels under 95% of the limit, h2 inside the band and both voltages in 1.3-11.8 V with Q on target, I return it unchanged, so a pump near saturation or an upper level approaching its limit only triggers the smallest move along the constant-production curve that restores feasibility.
proposed_change: Replace the fixed split recipe with a flow/disturbance estimator built from the upper-tank balances plus a feasibility-first search over the constant-production curve. The active setpoints are held unless their projected steady h3/h4, h2 band or pump voltage violates a margin, in which case the nearest feasible on-curve pair is returned.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The incremental delta-shift supervisor chases the upper-level slope term, causing continuous setpoint chattering during oscillatory disturbances. This injects level-tracking transients that drive production off target by ~0.4 L/s for hundreds of seconds. Independent clamping of h1 and h2 also breaks the constant-production relation, creating steady production error, and reaction to the slope term is too late for large steps so upper-level limits are exceeded.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Validate the new supervisor on held-out scenarios with different sine periods, phase, and amplitudes to confirm the steady-state prediction and hysteresis do not overfit the visible traces.

self_check: The supervisor estimates the current feed disturbances and effective pump gains from the lower and upper tank mass balances in the telemetry window, then predicts the steady-state h3, h4, v1, and v2 for any candidate setpoint pair on the constant-production curve. It moves only when the active setpoints are off target or their predicted constraints violate tiered margins, and it jumps directly to the minimal-travel feasible point, avoiding continuous chattering. When an upper level nears its limit, the scan shifts production away from the pump feeding that upper tank; when a pump approaches saturation, the scan reduces the corresponding lower-tank setpoint demand, keeping Q on target because the new pair stays on the constant-Q curve. Hysteresis holds the current setpoints whenever they remain feasible and on target, so oscillatory disturbances cause at most one clean move per half-cycle instead of repeated small steps.
proposed_change: Replace the heuristic incremental split shift and independent setpoint clamping with a one-dimensional scan along the constant-production curve that uses disturbances estimated from the window to predict h3, h4, v1, and v2 for each candidate. Choose the minimal-travel feasible point with tiered constraint margins and hold it whenever it remains feasible and on target.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor over-reacts to oscillating disturbances and transient upper-level slopes, moving the setpoints repeatedly; each move injects level-tracking transients that keep production off target (396 L off in dev_pump_sine_0, 332 L off in dev_feed_sine_0). It reacts too slowly to a sustained feed step, allowing h3/h4 to exceed 0.75 m for 113 s. Target changes trigger large unnecessary travel (0.63 m in nominal_target_up_0).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use the kinematic upper-level predictor and pump-voltage margins to hold setpoints unless a constraint is projected to violate; then shift only the production split along the Q=target contour, with a deadband and rate limit to avoid transients.

self_check: The supervisor predicts steady upper levels kinematically from current levels and slopes, so it shifts production only when a constraint is projected to breach its margin. Shifting along the Q=target curve keeps production on target, while a voltage margin of 10.5 V shifts load away from a saturating pump and prevents the associated production loss. A deadband and rate limit suppress chattering.
proposed_change: Replace the heuristic disturbance-driven shift with a kinematic steady-state upper-level predictor plus pump-voltage margins that hold the setpoints unless a projected violation occurs. When a violation is projected, shift the production split minimally along the constant-production curve, then apply a deadband and rate limit.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor over-reacts to transient upper-level trends during sinusoidal disturbances, continuously moving setpoints and causing production chattering; it also uses an overly conservative upper-level target (0.675) and damps the constrained split, delaying necessary shifts during step disturbances.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If further improvement is needed, add a mild proportional Q-error feedback on the setpoints to reduce production off-target during fast disturbances, carefully limited to avoid steady-state offset.

self_check: Our logic predicts steady-state upper levels from current inflow and only shifts production along the Q-target contour when the predicted level exceeds a margin 0.03 below the limit, avoiding transient reactions. Pump voltage limits enforce a shift away from a saturating pump. The full constrained split is applied without damping to quickly arrest step disturbances.
proposed_change: Raise the upper-level target from 0.675 to ulim-0.03 to suppress unnecessary shifts during sines, and remove the 0.8 damping factor so step violations are corrected fully in one call.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor holds setpoints too long and reacts only to instantaneous upper-level slack, so oscillatory feed/pump disturbances drive production off target and push upper levels to their limit; the lack of a steady-state production-split projection causes slow recovery and unnecessary travel.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use a steady-state constrained scan over the production split with online-estimated disturbances and effective pump gains, plus a production-error bias to correct tracking lag.

self_check: The steady-state scan evaluates each candidate split using estimated disturbances and pump coefficients to predict upper levels and voltages, rejecting infeasible points. If a pump approaches saturation or an upper level nears its limit, the cost penalizes it and the scan shifts production to the other tank. The Q-error bias moves setpoints along the target contour to correct PI lag, and the step limit prevents chattering.
proposed_change: Replace the heuristic delta shift with a steady-state constrained scan over the production split, using regression-based estimates of disturbances and effective pump gains. Add a production-error proportional bias to the scan target to compensate PI tracking lag.
